Task: Audit all 38 references against authoritative records
Why / Problem: A reference-integrity objection can sink the resubmission even when the technical contribution is sound.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Verify exact title, full author list, venue, year, pages and DOI/official record for every reference.
• Record an authoritative URL and the exact manuscript claim supported by each citation.
• Mark unresolved entries as 'Unverified' rather than assuming they exist.
Definition of Done: All 38 rows in Reference Audit have source URL, verification status and claim mapping.

Task: Resolve references [25] and [37] without prematurely calling them fabricated
Why / Problem: The current tracker labels them confirmed non-existent, but that conclusion must be based on an authoritative provenance search.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Search official proceedings, Crossref, DBLP, publisher libraries and author profiles.
• If no authoritative record is found, remove and replace them with real papers that support the exact claims.
• In the response, state the audit process and correction without speculating about how the error occurred.
Definition of Done: Each reference is either verified with an official record or removed and replaced with a claim-matched source.

Task: Re-evaluate reference [32] and the multi-timescale neuroscience claim
Why / Problem: Even if the paper exists, a real citation used for the wrong claim is still a scholarly accuracy problem.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Verify the paper's actual scope.
• Remove it from statements about multi-scale cognitive neurodynamics unless it directly supports them.
• Replace with a direct, authoritative multi-timescale cognition or neurodynamics source where needed.
Definition of Done: Every use of [32] accurately matches the source, or the reference is replaced.

Task: Verify the StudentLife citation [1] against the official ACM record
Why / Problem: The reviewer alleges an authorship problem; the response must rely on the official record, not memory.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Verify authors, exact title, page range and DOI/ACM record.
• Correct any title or author-order variation.
• Respond politely with the official record if the submitted citation was already correct.
Definition of Done: Reference [1] exactly matches the official bibliographic record.

Task: Build a claim-to-citation matrix for every strong literature claim
Why / Problem: Correct references are not enough; each citation must actually support the sentence attached to it.
Detailed Action Steps:
• List every novelty, neuroscience, dataset, baseline and convergence claim.
• Map each claim to one or more verified references.
• Delete or soften claims without direct support.
Definition of Done: All strong external claims are mapped to verified sources; unsupported claims are removed or softened.

Task: Create a table-and-figure provenance map from raw logs
Why / Problem: Every reported value must be traceable to a specific run, seed, config and output file.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Map every number in Tables 2–5 and Figures 4–11 to a run ID and log path.
• Record dataset split, seed, commit hash and configuration.
• Re-run or remove values that cannot be reproduced.
Definition of Done: Every result cell and figure has a traceable run ID and reproducible source file.

Task: Resolve Reviewer 1's alleged 58.7 versus 68.7 mismatch correctly
Why / Problem: The submitted Table 2 shows 68.7, so this appears to be a reviewer reading/rendering issue, not a data discrepancy.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Confirm the source logs still produce 68.7 ± 2.3.
• Improve Table 2 resolution and typography.
• In the response, quote the exact row and explain that the manuscript text and table are consistent.
Definition of Done: The value is reproduced from logs and the response politely documents the table's actual value.
Deliverable / Evidence: Reproduced run + high-resolution table + rebuttal text

Task: Reconfirm the generative-AI disclosure is literally accurate
Why / Problem: The final manuscript must accurately describe how AI tools were used, especially after the reference audit.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Document the actual use of AI tools in drafting, coding, analysis and editing.
• Align the disclosure with IEEE policy and the real workflow.
• Obtain coauthor approval of the final wording.
Definition of Done: The disclosure is factually accurate, policy-aligned and approved by all authors.

Task: Freeze and archive the exact code, configs and data manifests used for revision
Why / Problem: A stable evidence package prevents silent changes while the response and manuscript are being updated.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Create a tagged Git commit for the revision.
• Save environment file, package versions, random seeds and data checksums.
• Archive raw logs and plotting scripts in a read-only folder.
Definition of Done: A tagged, checksum-backed revision archive can reproduce all reported outputs.
Deliverable / Evidence: Git tag + environment lockfile + data/log manifest

Task: Conduct a coauthor integrity sign-off before technical revision proceeds
Why / Problem: Both authors should agree that references, results and disclosures are accurate before investing in new experiments.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Review the completed reference and result audits together.
• Document unresolved items and owners.
• Record written approval to proceed.
Definition of Done: Guide/coauthor signs off on the integrity gate with no unresolved P0 issue.

Task: Decide: obtain true multi-node results or reframe as single-server multi-GPU
Why / Problem: Bandwidth throttling on one NVLink server does not validate physical multi-node behavior.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Option A: run on at least 2–4 physical hosts and report NIC, topology, RTT, bandwidth and variance.
• Option B: explicitly reframe the contribution as branch-parallel multi-GPU execution and remove physical-cluster claims.
• Record the decision before rewriting the title or abstract.
Definition of Done: A written scope decision is approved by the guide and reflected consistently across the manuscript.
Deliverable / Evidence: Decision Log entry + approved scope statement
Manuscript Section: Title; Abstract; Sections I, IV-E, V, VIII, IX

Task: Decide how to address the small-dataset versus population-scale mismatch
Why / Problem: StudentLife and DAIC-WOZ do not themselves demonstrate a need for population-scale distributed training.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Add honest synthetic or replicated longitudinal workloads for scaling analysis, or
• Remove 'thousands of participants' and population-scale validation language.
• Separate modeling validation from systems scalability validation.
Definition of Done: The motivation and evidence are aligned without overstating what the datasets prove.

Task: Formally validate whether standard DDP inherently violates temporal causality in this setup
Why / Problem: Causal ordering inside a complete sequence is not automatically violated merely because gradients from different samples are aggregated.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Define the exact sample unit, windowing, state carry-over and asynchronous update process.
• Identify the mechanism by which DDP would create causal inconsistency.
• Design controlled experiments that isolate this mechanism from batch size, sampler, learning-rate and seed effects.
Definition of Done: The paper either proves and experimentally isolates a specific causality failure mode, or removes the general claim.
Deliverable / Evidence: Formal problem definition + controlled experiment specification

Task: Decide whether Theorem 1 is retained, replaced or removed
Why / Problem: The current proof sketch does not establish convergence of a causally masked, biased gradient estimator.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Retain only if a mathematically valid bounded-bias/asynchronous proof is completed and independently reviewed.
• Otherwise replace the theorem with a proposition that states an operational staleness bound, without a convergence claim.
• Ensure the empirical evidence matches the reduced claim.
Definition of Done: The theorem status is approved by a qualified reviewer and reflected consistently in text, algorithm and response.

Task: Obtain guide approval on the revised paper identity before new writing
Why / Problem: Editing before the core decisions are settled creates contradictory versions and wasted work.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Review D1-01 through D1-07 with the guide.
• Record selected options and rejected alternatives.
• Lock the scope for the remainder of the revision.
Definition of Done: Guide marks all structural decisions approved in the Decision Log.

Task: Derive and verify the exact receptive field for each branch
Why / Problem: Equation (2) appears to contain two dilated convolutions per block, so neither the manuscript values nor the reviewer's one-convolution calculation should be adopted without verification.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Derive the formula from the implemented block, including both convolutions, padding and residual path.
• Write a unit test that perturbs input positions and measures the effective receptive field.
• Correct Figure 2, text and temporal-unit labels from the verified result.
Definition of Done: Analytical derivation and code-based measurement agree for all branches.

Task: Rewrite the staleness counter semantics
Why / Problem: The current increment/reset behavior is not clearly consistent with the prose description of continuously bounded staleness.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Define precisely what Δ_b counts: optimizer steps, parameter versions or missed synchronizations.
• Specify when it increments and resets.
• Make Algorithm 1 and Section III-D identical in meaning.
Definition of Done: A reader can simulate the counter without ambiguity, and the code follows the same rule.

Task: Explain HOLD-triggered synchronization versus periodic AllReduce
Why / Problem: Two synchronization paths are present but their interaction, ordering and parameter scope are unclear.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Specify whether HOLD synchronizes one branch or the full model.
• Define precedence when HOLD and periodic synchronization occur in the same step.
• Measure the communication and optimization consequences.
Definition of Done: The algorithm, pseudocode and implementation use one unambiguous synchronization protocol.

Task: Define TCP behavior when branches are replicated for N > 3
Why / Problem: The paper introduces data-parallel branch replicas without explaining how their gradients are synchronized under TCP.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Specify intra-replica and inter-branch aggregation order.
• State whether causal masking applies before or after replica reduction.
• Remove N > 3 claims if the implemented behavior is not defined and tested.
Definition of Done: A complete execution graph exists for N=4, 8 and any reported higher count.

Task: Explain how N = 16 was produced on an eight-GPU server
Why / Problem: The hardware description and scalability table are currently inconsistent.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Document whether N means process, virtual worker, branch replica or physical GPU.
• Describe oversubscription if used.
• Remove or relabel N=16 results if they do not represent 16 independent compute resources.
Definition of Done: Node/worker/GPU terminology is consistent and every N value is physically interpretable.

Task: State all assumptions required by the revised theoretical result
Why / Problem: The current proof sketch omits assumptions about estimator bias, delay, bounded gradients and synchronization.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Define objective, stochastic estimator, masking operator and parameter-delay model.
• State smoothness, variance/bias and bounded-delay assumptions.
• Explain which assumptions are empirically checkable.
Definition of Done: The theorem/proposition is self-contained and every symbol and assumption is defined.

Task: Complete a valid proof or explicitly remove the convergence guarantee
Why / Problem: Causal masking creates a potentially biased estimator that cannot simply inherit an unbiased asynchronous-SGD theorem.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Derive a bounded-bias result using an appropriate theorem, or provide a fresh proof.
• Analyze the HOLD and periodic-sync interaction.
• Have a qualified colleague independently review every step.
Definition of Done: Independent reviewer signs off on the proof, or all convergence-guarantee language is removed.
Deliverable / Evidence: Reviewed appendix proof or approved replacement text

Task: Audit StudentLife split for participant leakage
Why / Problem: 'Participant-stratified' can mean either subject-independent splitting or the same subjects appearing in train and test.
Detailed Action Steps:
• List subject IDs in each split.
• Use a subject-independent evaluation for generalization claims.
• If within-subject evaluation is retained, label it clearly and avoid unseen-subject claims.
Definition of Done: Split membership is documented and no hidden subject overlap remains.

Task: Clarify and correct the DAIC-WOZ 107/82 split
Why / Problem: The common partition is 107 train, 35 development and 47 test; merging or relabeling requires explicit justification and label availability.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Document exactly which official partitions and labels were used.
• Explain whether development and test were combined.
• Prefer a standard, reproducible evaluation split and re-run results if necessary.
Definition of Done: The split is standard or fully justified, reproducible and comparable with prior work.
Deliverable / Evidence: Split manifest + rerun results if changed

Task: Define how subject embeddings are handled for held-out and unseen subjects
Why / Problem: A learned identity embedding can leak test-subject information if trained using all subject IDs.
Detailed Action Steps:
• State whether test subjects appear during training.
• Add an unknown-subject baseline and a support-set adaptation protocol.
• Separate within-subject personalization from unseen-subject generalization.
Definition of Done: No test-subject identity information is used improperly; cold-start performance is measured.

Task: Audit forward-fill and imputation for temporal leakage
Why / Problem: Imputation across split boundaries or from future observations can inflate performance.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Fit and apply imputation separately within each split and sequence.
• Prohibit backward information flow.
• Report missingness and imputation sensitivity.
Definition of Done: No preprocessing step uses future or test-set information.

Task: Audit fairness of all baseline configurations
Why / Problem: A 1.1-point DDP degradation cannot support a causal claim unless batch size, optimizer and sampler confounders are controlled.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Match effective global batch size or report it explicitly.
• Tune learning rate for each effective batch size.
• Use identical data splits, preprocessing, early stopping and seed schedule.
Definition of Done: Baseline differences cannot be explained by avoidable training-protocol mismatches.

Task: Run controlled DDP experiments that isolate the proposed temporal-inconsistency mechanism
Why / Problem: The current comparison does not establish that temporal causality, rather than optimization configuration, causes degradation.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Compare DDP with matched global batch size and tuned learning rate.
• Compare random versus chronological window assignment.
• Compare stateful versus stateless sequence handling and overlap/no-overlap conditions.
Definition of Done: The specific failure mode is isolated with controls, or the general DDP-causality claim is withdrawn.

Task: Run true multi-node experiments if the distributed scope is retained
Why / Problem: Physical hosts introduce network stack, NIC, congestion, NUMA and straggler effects absent from NVLink emulation.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Use at least 2 and preferably 4 physical hosts.
• Report GPU, CPU, NIC, topology, RTT, bandwidth, software stack and repeated runs.
• Include DDP and D-MSTCN under identical conditions.
Definition of Done: At least one genuine multi-node result supports every retained physical-cluster claim.

Task: Evaluate personalization for unseen subjects
Why / Problem: The main deployment target includes new subjects who have no learned embedding.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Evaluate a global/unknown embedding.
• Evaluate few-shot adaptation with a clearly separated support set.
• Report seen-subject and unseen-subject results separately.
Definition of Done: Cold-start behavior is quantified and no hidden test-subject training occurs.

Task: Redesign the significance-testing plan
Why / Problem: With only five paired observations, an exact two-sided Wilcoxon test cannot produce p < 0.05 even when all differences have the same sign.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Increase independent runs for headline comparisons, preferably to at least 10.
• Report exact test type, alternative hypothesis, statistic and p-value.
• Use confidence intervals and effect sizes; correct for multiple comparisons where applicable.
Definition of Done: Every significance symbol can be independently reproduced and is statistically valid.

Task: Rewrite title and abstract after the structural decisions and reruns
Why / Problem: The abstract currently combines modeling, theory and cluster-scale claims more strongly than the evidence supports.
Detailed Action Steps:
• State the exact experimental environment.
• Report only validated headline numbers.
• Remove or bound unsupported novelty and convergence claims.
Definition of Done: Every abstract sentence is directly supported by the revised manuscript.

Task: Rewrite the temporal-causality problem statement narrowly and formally
Why / Problem: The current prose treats temporally distinct gradients as inherently non-exchangeable without defining the conditions.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Use the formal definition from D1-03.
• State the conditions under which the problem arises.
• Avoid generalizing to all temporal models or all DDP training.
Definition of Done: The problem statement is technically precise and matches the controlled experiments.

Task: Create a reviewer-comment master matrix
Why / Problem: Eight reviewers create a high risk of silently missing a comment.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Copy each comment verbatim or faithfully summarize it.
• Map it to task IDs, manuscript locations and evidence.
• Mark accept, partially accept or respectfully rebut.
Definition of Done: Every reviewer comment appears exactly once with an assigned response and action.

Task: Write the formal response-to-reviewers document
Why / Problem: IEEE Access requires concern, response and action for every comment.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Use a professional, non-defensive tone.
• Lead with changes and evidence.
• For rebuttals, provide exact table/equation/page evidence.
Definition of Done: All reviewer comments have complete concern-response-action entries.

Task: Produce the highlighted-changes PDF
Why / Problem: The editor requests every individual change, including grammar, to be highlighted.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Generate from the final source.
• Check that highlights do not hide equations or figures.
• Verify it matches the clean manuscript.
Definition of Done: Highlighted PDF is complete, readable and content-identical to the clean manuscript.

Task: Produce the clean LaTeX/Word source and PDF
Why / Problem: IEEE requires clean source and PDF as the main manuscript.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Compile from the locked revision tag.
• Remove comments, highlights and tracked-change artifacts.
• Verify bibliography and supplementary references.
Definition of Done: Clean source compiles without warnings that affect content, and PDF passes QA.

Task: Complete the IEEE Access resubmission checklist
Why / Problem: The resubmission is one-shot; administrative omissions can waste the technical revision.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Work through each checklist item.
• Confirm file names and submission categories.
• Confirm whether any author-list change form is needed.
Definition of Done: Every checklist item is completed and signed off.

Task: Run an independent internal re-review against the original reviewer comments
Why / Problem: The revised paper should be tested as though the same reviewers will return.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Give the clean manuscript, response and supplement to a colleague not involved in drafting.
• Ask them to find any unresolved comment, unsupported claim or inconsistency.
• Close every red-team finding.
Definition of Done: Independent reviewer signs off that all comments are addressed.

Task: Obtain final guide and coauthor approval
Why / Problem: The guide should approve the paper's scope, proof status, reference corrections and response tone.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Review final files together.
• Confirm author contributions and disclosure.
• Record approval before upload.
Definition of Done: All authors approve the exact files to be submitted.

Task: Create a final immutable submission archive before upload
Why / Problem: A one-shot resubmission needs an exact backup of what was submitted.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Zip all source files, PDFs, supplement, response and checklist.
• Include checksums and a contents manifest.
• Save the portal confirmation after submission.
Definition of Done: The exact submission can be reconstructed from the archive.

Task: Define the single strongest methodological novelty
Why / Problem: The paper currently reads as a combination of known components unless the new mechanism is isolated precisely.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Name the closest methods and state the exact technical difference.
• Separate architectural novelty, systems novelty and application novelty.
• Avoid claiming novelty merely because components are combined.
Definition of Done: A 3–5 sentence novelty statement survives comparison with the closest prior work.
Deliverable / Evidence: Approved novelty statement + comparison table outline

Task: Select a title that matches the final evidence
Why / Problem: The current title implies distributed scalability beyond what a single-server experiment establishes.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Prepare title options for both scope outcomes.
• Avoid 'scalable' or 'distributed' if the evidence is limited to one host.
• Obtain guide approval after D1-01 through D1-05 are closed.
Definition of Done: Final title makes no claim that the revised experiments do not support.

Task: Create a manuscript-wide claim-strength policy
Why / Problem: Statements such as 'first', 'guarantees', 'near-linear' and 'population-scale' carry a high evidence burden.
Detailed Action Steps:
• List all strong claim words.
• Define evidence required to retain each one.
• Replace unsupported claims with measured, bounded statements.
Definition of Done: No strong claim remains without a corresponding proof, experiment or authoritative literature basis.

Task: Remove η notation overloading
Why / Problem: η is used for both learning rate and scalability efficiency.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Reserve η for scalability efficiency.
• Use a distinct symbol such as α_lr for learning rate.
• Search equations, tables, captions and prose for every occurrence.
Definition of Done: Each symbol has one meaning throughout the manuscript.
Manuscript Section: Sections III-D, IV-C, IV-F; Tables 1 and 3

Task: Correct the personalization-adapter parameter count
Why / Problem: The shared matrices contribute O(D²) parameters; the per-subject cost is the embedding dimension d_s, not 2D.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Compute exact shared and per-subject parameter counts from code.
• Update the equations and complexity discussion.
• Replace 'negligible' with measured overhead.
Definition of Done: Parameter counts in prose, table and code summary match exactly.

Task: Replace universal EEG-timescale grounding with dataset-specific temporal rationale
Why / Problem: Minute-resolution smartphone data cannot resolve theta- or alpha-band oscillations.
Detailed Action Steps:
• State actual sampling intervals and receptive-field durations for each dataset.
• Present the schedules as heuristic multi-resolution choices unless directly grounded for that dataset.
• Reserve EEG-frequency discussion for SEED or other truly high-frequency data.
Definition of Done: Every temporal-scale statement is physically meaningful for the dataset being discussed.

Task: Expand the analytical computational and communication complexity derivation
Why / Problem: The paper currently gives only a coarse operation expression and communication estimate.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Derive time and memory complexity per branch and for CSAG/adapter/head.
• Separate forward, backward and synchronization costs.
• Relate formulas to measured values.
Definition of Done: Analytical estimates and measured profiling results are reported together.

Task: Add unit and integration tests for TCP, SAP, receptive field and parameter counts
Why / Problem: Several reviewer concerns are symptoms of undocumented implementation behavior.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Test counter transitions and synchronization ordering.
• Test SAP placement and N>3 replication.
• Test receptive fields and exact parameter counts.
Definition of Done: Automated tests pass on the tagged revision commit and are included in the repository.

Task: Document the complete preprocessing pipeline
Why / Problem: Reproducibility requires exact resampling, normalization, feature extraction and window construction details.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Specify software versions and parameters.
• Fit normalization only on training data.
• Publish scripts or pseudocode for every transformation.
Definition of Done: A new researcher can reproduce the model inputs from the raw/public data.

Task: Audit overlapping windows and duplicate temporal content across splits
Why / Problem: Highly overlapping windows can place nearly identical observations in training and test sets.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Measure overlap between windows across splits.
• Split by subject/session before window generation where possible.
• Document exclusion gaps if needed.
Definition of Done: Train and test examples do not share overlapping raw intervals.

Task: Report class distributions and imbalance handling
Why / Problem: Macro F1 alone does not show whether rare classes or thresholds drive the gains.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Report train/validation/test counts by class and subject.
• Document weighting or sampling.
• Add per-class precision, recall and F1.
Definition of Done: Class balance and per-class results are fully reported.

Task: Specify seeds, determinism settings and repeated-run protocol
Why / Problem: Reported variance is meaningful only when the source of randomness and run protocol are controlled.
Detailed Action Steps:
• List all seeds.
• Document deterministic/non-deterministic CUDA settings.
• Use the same seed schedule across baselines.
Definition of Done: Every experiment has a documented, repeatable seed and environment policy.

Task: Reconcile subjects, sessions, windows and labelled-sample counts
Why / Problem: Scalability motivation can be distorted if sample counts and sequence lengths are not clearly separated.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Report subjects, sessions, windows, sequence-length distribution and total timesteps.
• Clarify whether samples are independent.
• Use these values in the compute-motivation discussion.
Definition of Done: Dataset-scale claims use precise and consistent units.

Task: Add synthetic or replicated longitudinal workloads at larger scale
Why / Problem: Public cognitive datasets are too small to test the systems motivation directly.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Create transparent synthetic workloads varying participants, sequence length and feature count.
• Preserve the model's compute and communication characteristics.
• Clearly separate synthetic scalability from predictive-validity claims.
Definition of Done: Scaling behavior is evaluated across a workload range that stresses the system.

Task: Benchmark bandwidth, RTT, jitter, packet loss and straggler sensitivity
Why / Problem: Bandwidth alone does not model real distributed execution.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Test a matrix of RTT and bandwidth values.
• Inject controlled stragglers and jitter.
• Report mean, variance and tail latency.
Definition of Done: The paper quantifies where the approach helps and where it fails.

Task: Repeat throughput and efficiency measurements
Why / Problem: Single-run wall-clock values are insufficient for systems claims.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Run warm-up iterations.
• Repeat each configuration at least 5–10 times.
• Report mean, standard deviation and 95% confidence intervals.
Definition of Done: All scaling metrics include run count, variance and confidence intervals.

Task: Report parameters, FLOPs, peak GPU memory and inference latency
Why / Problem: Reviewers need a complete cost-versus-quality comparison.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Profile D-MSTCN and all major baselines with the same input shapes.
• Report batch and single-sample latency.
• Separate training and inference costs.
Definition of Done: A complete computational-profile table is included and reproducible.

Task: Ablate alternative dilation schedules
Why / Problem: Fixed schedules are central to the multi-scale claim but are insufficiently tested.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Test at least two alternative schedules.
• Include a learned or data-adaptive schedule if feasible.
• Report accuracy, compute and receptive-field duration.
Definition of Done: The chosen schedules are empirically justified rather than assumed.

Task: Ablate number of branches and kernel sizes
Why / Problem: The contribution of three branches and K=3 should be demonstrated.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Evaluate 1-, 2-, 3- and 4-branch variants where practical.
• Compare K=3 and K=5.
• Report parameter-matched variants when possible.
Definition of Done: Architecture choices are supported by controlled ablations.

Task: Compare CSAG with alternative fusion mechanisms
Why / Problem: Fixed averaging alone is not a broad comparison of attention-based fusion choices.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Compare concatenation+MLP, scalar gating and one alternative attention mechanism.
• Match parameter counts where feasible.
• Analyze stability and interpretability.
Definition of Done: CSAG's benefit is established against credible alternatives.

Task: Compare FiLM with lightweight personalization alternatives
Why / Problem: The choice of FiLM needs an accuracy, parameter and adaptation-cost justification.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Add a plain adapter baseline.
• Add LoRA where architecturally meaningful.
• Add a simple fine-tuning or meta-learning baseline if resources permit.
Definition of Done: FiLM is justified by a measured tradeoff, not convenience alone.

Task: Re-run headline comparisons with sufficient seeds
Why / Problem: The current five-seed design has low power and cannot support some stated significance claims.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Use the same seed list for D-MSTCN and key baselines.
• Prioritize D-MSTCN N=1, D-MSTCN scaled, iTransformer, Temporal-CNN and DDP-LSTM.
• Report all runs, including failures.
Definition of Done: Headline results have adequate repeated runs and transparent exclusions.

Task: Add 95% confidence intervals and effect sizes
Why / Problem: Mean ± standard deviation does not directly communicate uncertainty or practical magnitude.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Compute bootstrap or appropriate parametric confidence intervals.
• Report effect size for key pairwise comparisons.
• Avoid over-interpreting small F1 differences.
Definition of Done: Main quality and systems results include uncertainty and practical effect magnitude.

Task: Expand δ_max and T_sync sensitivity analysis
Why / Problem: The protocol's behavior depends on two interacting synchronization controls.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Run a grid over δ_max and T_sync.
• Report F1, throughput, communication and synchronization frequency.
• Relate the empirical tradeoff to any retained theory.
Definition of Done: Default settings are justified and interaction effects are visible.

Task: Validate communication-volume calculations with instrumentation
Why / Problem: Analytical byte counts can miss protocol overhead and repeated synchronization.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Instrument NCCL/process communication.
• Compare measured and analytical bytes.
• Report per-step and per-epoch totals.
Definition of Done: Communication claims are backed by measured values and an explained calculation.

Task: Prepare an anonymized code and reproducibility package before resubmission
Why / Problem: A concrete artifact strengthens the response to reproducibility concerns.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Include configs, environment, preprocessing and plotting scripts.
• Provide a minimal reproduction command.
• Respect dataset redistribution restrictions.
Definition of Done: A reviewer-accessible repository or archive reproduces at least the main results.

Task: Rewrite the contribution list as falsifiable, evidence-backed statements
Why / Problem: A contribution should describe what is new and what was demonstrated, not promise a broad capability.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Separate architecture, protocol, partitioning, personalization and evaluation.
• Remove items that are not independently novel.
• Attach each contribution to a section and result.
Definition of Done: Each contribution has a precise implementation and evaluation trail.

Task: Add a closest-method comparison table
Why / Problem: The novelty is easier to assess when neighboring approaches are compared feature by feature.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Include multi-scale temporal models, distributed/pipeline methods, asynchronous training and personalization.
• Use only verified references.
• Compare objective, temporal scales, distribution mode, consistency mechanism and personalization.
Definition of Done: The reader can see the precise gap addressed by the revised method.

Task: Remove or substantiate all 'first' and 'guarantee' language
Why / Problem: Unsupported superlatives invite a second rejection under binary review.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Search for first, novel, guarantee, scalable, near-linear, causal and population-scale.
• Retain only with direct evidence.
• Use measured scope and limitations.
Definition of Done: Claim audit shows zero unsupported superlatives.

Task: Expand the limitations section with concrete boundaries
Why / Problem: The paper acknowledges limitations but still makes broader claims elsewhere.
Detailed Action Steps:
• State hardware limits, dataset scale, cold start, fixed schedules and aggregator bottleneck.
• Add the limitations of simulated networking if retained.
• Explain what the results do not establish.
Definition of Done: Limitations are specific, consistent with the claims and referenced in the conclusion.

Task: Add a practical deployment discussion
Why / Problem: Reviewers asked for latency, communication, unseen subjects and operational constraints.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Describe training and inference topology separately.
• Discuss new-subject onboarding, failure handling and privacy boundaries.
• Tie deployment statements to measured latency and communication.
Definition of Done: Deployment guidance is concrete and does not exceed the evaluated setting.

Task: Rewrite the conclusion to match the final scope
Why / Problem: The conclusion repeats the strongest distributed and theoretical claims.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Report only revised numbers.
• Separate demonstrated findings from future work.
• Remove claims withdrawn during structural decisions.
Definition of Done: Conclusion contains no claim absent from the revised evidence.

Task: Prepare a respectful rebuttal to the 58.7 reading error
Why / Problem: The reviewer concern should be corrected without sounding adversarial.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Thank the reviewer for prompting verification.
• State that both text and Table 2 show 68.7 ± 2.3.
• Mention the new provenance audit and improved table resolution.
Definition of Done: Response includes evidence, action and page/line references.

Task: Add page, section and line references to every reviewer response
Why / Problem: A response is persuasive only when the editor can locate the exact change quickly.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Use one concern-response-action block per comment.
• Quote the revised wording where useful.
• Record page and line numbers after final typesetting.
Definition of Done: Every response item points to an exact location and deliverable.

Task: Re-export architectural diagrams and algorithms as vector graphics
Why / Problem: Blurred equations and labels impair technical review.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Use PDF/SVG/vector output where supported.
• Ensure fonts are embedded and notation matches the text.
• Check at single-column and double-column print size.
Definition of Done: Figures 1–3 and Algorithm 1 are crisp and legible at final size.

Task: Run a similarity check on the final manuscript
Why / Problem: A large rewrite can still contain accidental overlap from source wording or prior versions.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Review flagged passages manually.
• Fix inappropriate verbatim overlap.
• Do not distort standard technical phrases merely to lower a score.
Definition of Done: No unresolved inappropriate textual overlap remains.

Task: Verify portal metadata against the manuscript
Why / Problem: Title, abstract, authors, ORCID, keywords and affiliations must be identical across files and portal.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Compare every field.
• Verify corresponding-author email and ORCID.
• Confirm no accidental author-order change.
Definition of Done: Portal and manuscript metadata match exactly.

Task: Perform a two-person portal review before clicking submit
Why / Problem: Wrong file categories or stale uploads can invalidate otherwise correct work.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Open every uploaded file from the portal preview.
• Check file type/category and version.
• Have the guide or coauthor verify before final submission.
Definition of Done: Two people confirm the portal package is correct before submission.

Task: Confirm dataset permissions, ethics statements and clinical-claim boundaries
Why / Problem: Cognitive and depression modeling require careful wording about screening versus diagnosis.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Verify data-use terms.
• State that outputs are research classifications, not clinical diagnoses.
• Update ethics and limitations language.
Definition of Done: Data-use and clinical-boundary statements are accurate and complete.

Task: Qualify the CSAG attention interpretation
Why / Problem: Attention weights can be descriptive without proving causal importance.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Describe them as post-hoc model behavior.
• Avoid equating attention with explanation or mechanism.
• Cross-reference ablation evidence.
Definition of Done: Interpretability wording is cautious and evidence-aligned.

Task: Handle the alleged Algorithm 1 'date' typo as a rendering clarification
Why / Problem: The submitted PDF shows Δ_b += 1; the response should still acknowledge readability issues.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Verify the source and compiled PDF.
• Improve vector rendering.
• State politely that the operator was present and has been made clearer.
Definition of Done: Response resolves the concern and the revised algorithm is unmistakably legible.

Task: Evaluate Reviewer 5's suggested citations individually
Why / Problem: Suggested references should be added only if they genuinely support the revised paper.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Read each paper.
• Map it to a specific manuscript claim or decline it politely.
• Never add citations solely to appease the reviewer.
Definition of Done: Each suggested reference has a documented include/decline decision.

Task: Remove the 'VOLUME 4, 2016' placeholder throughout
Why / Problem: The placeholder signals insufficient final quality control.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Correct the IEEE Access template/footer.
• Inspect every page in the final PDF.
Definition of Done: No placeholder remains in source or PDF.

Task: Fix Table 2 and Table 5 headers and labels
Why / Problem: Garbled labels reduce trust and caused at least one reviewer misreading.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Use 'Comm. (MB/epoch)' or an equally clear header.
• Use explicit ablation labels such as 'w/o MSB'.
• Increase table text size and spacing.
Definition of Done: All tables are readable at 100% zoom and in print.

Task: Standardize table and figure notation
Why / Problem: Inconsistent abbreviations and symbols make the paper harder to audit.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Define every abbreviation in captions.
• Use the same node/worker/GPU terminology.
• Standardize decimal places and uncertainty notation.
Definition of Done: Captions and tables use consistent terms, symbols and precision.

Task: Run a full notation, grammar and cross-reference audit
Why / Problem: The revision will introduce many new equations, tables and sections.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Check equation, figure, table and section references.
• Check symbol definitions and tense.
• Use a final human review after any language tool.
Definition of Done: No broken cross-reference, undefined symbol or visible grammar issue remains.

Task: Inspect the final PDF at 100%, 150% and print view
Why / Problem: Many reviewer concerns were amplified by rendering quality.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Inspect every page.
• Check clipping, font embedding, equations, legends and tables.
• Verify the highlighted version has the same pagination as the clean version where possible.
Definition of Done: A page-by-page PDF QA checklist is complete with zero unresolved issue.

Task: Prepare a structured supplementary appendix
Why / Problem: A full proof, extended experiments and reproducibility details may not fit cleanly in the main article.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Include proof or proposition details.
• Include additional tables, hyperparameters and run protocols.
• Cross-reference the supplement from the main text and response.
Definition of Done: Supplement is complete, numbered and consistent with the main manuscript.

Task: Complete the guide's author biography
Why / Problem: The biography currently omits the Ph.D. field.
Detailed Action Steps:
• Confirm the exact degree field and institution.
• Update the biography with the guide's approval.
Definition of Done: Biography is complete and approved.
